reception: In the citing literature Dr. Memory serves chiefly as a yardstick. Memory-error detectors that followed — AddressSanitizer and MemorySanitizer among them — measure their speed and coverage against it, and the pattern repeats across use-after-free detection, uninitialized-read mitigation, firmware fuzzing, and shadow-memory monitoring. A second, larger body of citations places the tool in the standard roster of memory checkers, while binary-only fuzzing work puts the tool itself to use. Few papers build on its internals; its role in the literature is that of an established baseline against which new detectors are measured. The implementation lives on in the DynamoRIO/drmemory repository.
